key_insight: Matrix-product-state (MPS) encoding makes non-local pseudopotentials practical in first-quantized quantum simulation by lowering circuit depth for Trotter steps.
engineering_relevance: This is a useful route toward cheaper quantum chemistry and atomistic simulations on near-term hardware because it reduces gate overhead without abandoning first-quantized representations.
method: Encode the wave function with MPS to represent non-local projector terms efficiently.
Decompose the Trotter step using MPS-based operations for local and pseudopotential parts.
Apply the method to 1D hydrogen-ionization under an ultrashort laser pulse as a proof of concept.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a circuit-depth scaling of O(deg(V_loc) n^deg(V_loc) + 8Lnn_atomχ^2 + 2n^2) and states that the MPS approach significantly reduces depth versus direct unitary decomposition in the hydrogen-atom benchmark.
watch_item: Performance depends on the MPS bond dimension χ and the complexity of the pseudopotentials, so large entanglement or many projectors may still limit efficiency.
paper_title: First-quantized quantum simulation with non-local potentials by matrix-product-state encoding
